Marco (marketing): Heads-up — prepping Friday webinar (live demo + slides). Need a small, reproducible benchmark pack: cold-start heatmap, warmup vs no-warmup, and quantized (4-bit/8-bit) smoke runs for the model variants we'll list below. Can runtime run these and drop raw artifacts + a short method note? cc @Jordan @Sasha
Jordan (eng-runtime): Yep. Which model variants and exact prompt mix? Also: what metrics (p50/p95/p99, tokens/s, cold-start TTFB) and sample sizes do you want? We need target sequence length distribution + batch sizes to match marketing claims.
Marco (marketing): Primary: open-model-3b-v1 (float16), open-model-3b-q4, open-model-3b-q8. Prompt mix: 60% short queries (~16 tokens), 30% medium (~64), 10% long (~512). Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side), cold-start TTFB heatmap, tokens/sec, and variance across 50 runs. Need raw request payloads + seed info and the warmup policy used. Sample payloads below.
Marco (marketing): ```json
[
  {"id":"s1","prompt":"Summarize the following paragraph...","len":18},
  {"id":"m1","prompt":"Write a short email to a customer about...","len":72},
  {"id":"l1","prompt":"Given the following document, extract key takeaways and action items...","len":512}
]
```
Sasha (eng-runtime): Thanks. We'll run a smoke matrix: hosted/quantized/dedicated x warmup(0/1x32tokens) x batch sizes [1,4,8]. Quick clarifying Qs: 1) do you want KV cache persisted between runs? 2) should we include our client-side warmup script (recommended) or strictly raw cold starts?
Marco (marketing): Prefer both: raw cold starts and client-warmup-1x32 as separate lanes. KV cache: disabled for cold lanes, enabled for warmup lanes. Priority: high — need artifacts and a 1-paragraph method blurb by Wed EOD for slides.
Jordan (eng-runtime): Got it. We'll schedule. I'll spin runs with these params and attach a minimal runbook snippet and the raw logs. Run config we'll use: ```yaml
model: open-model-3b
variants: [float16, q4, q8]
traffic_profile: [60:16,30:64,10:512]
batch_sizes: [1,4,8]
warmup: [0, 1x32]
repeats: 50
metrics: [p50,p95,p99,ttfb,tokens_per_sec]
```
runtime-bot: Run queued: R-3323456789-quicksmoke. Owner: eng-runtime. Expected duration ~3h. Artifacts will be uploaded to: s3://redwood-benchmarks/R-3323456789/
DevOps (infra): Note: for quantized variants on hosted lane we might hit capacity; if that happens we'll fallback to a compatible dedicated node and mark that in metadata.
Marco (marketing): Thanks — please tag any runs that used dedicated fallback; we need to label claims appropriately in the deck. Also include the warmup script we run so marketing can reproduce locally.
Sasha (eng-runtime): Will do. Quick note: deterministic tokenization requires setting seed and tokenizer version; we'll include tokenizer sha and seed in the artifacts. Also we'll run a small reproducibility check: rerun 5 samples with identical seeds to verify determinism.
Marco (marketing): Perfect. Can you confirm Wed EOD timeline? Demo Friday morning.
Jordan (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. We'll prioritize the queue and ping here once artifacts are uploaded. If anything blocks (capacity or flaky quantized runs) we'll call a canary rerun.
runtime-bot: Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-benchmarks/R-3323456789/summary.json (ops + raw logs) — 3h 12m elapsed.
Sasha (eng-runtime): Uploaded method note (short): what we ran, traffic profile, warmup policy, seed/tokenizer, fallback notes. Also added a small script examples/run_smoke.sh in the bucket.
Marco (marketing): Amazing — thank you all. I'll review and draft the slide blurb. If we need tighter numbers we'll ask for a follow-up rerun but this should be enough for the first pass. :thumbsup:
